lyric: Verse 2: "I feel like no one wants me / And I hate the way I'm perceived"
lyric_idea: Line 1 (no one wants me) -> young job seekers and AI-era hiring rejections. Line 2 (the way I'm perceived) -> deepfakes of real people and video-call impersonation. Recommended pairing: SignalFire stat on the 'no one wants me' beat, then the Common Sense 67% deepfake stat or the CNN deepfake-CFO headline on the 'perceived' beat. Verified alternate: CNN 2024-05-16 'British engineering giant Arup revealed as $25 million deepfake scam victim' (https://www.cnn.com/2024/05/16/tech/arup-deepfake-scam-loss-hong-kong-intl-hnk/index.html). Verified alternate: Tavus Griffin '48%' stat (https://www.tavus.io/griffin; local stills in assets/research/work/video-tavus-griffin-*.jpg).

candidates.text: New grad/entry-level hiring has collapsed further: down roughly 65% at the Tech Majors and down ~76% at early stage startups compared to 2019.

candidates.verified_how: Page opened live (fetch) today; the '~76%' early-stage startup sentence is in the body text. Deck source: tools/slides_work.js, new-grad hiring stat '-76%' 'New-grad hiring at early-stage startups vs 2019' and source line naming SignalFire. Local chart images verified present and listed in deck manifest (quality 5).
candidates.why_it_fits: Plain, big number that reads in about 2 s on a phone and maps directly to 'no one wants me' for young job seekers. It is a market-wide hiring stat, not an AI-hiring stat; the deck's own honest caveat applies (part of the decline predates AI and reflects post-2022 over-hiring and rates). Show the source line on screen.
candidates.on_screen: ~76% + 'New-grad hiring at early-stage startups vs 2019' (the deck shows '-76%'; the source says '~76%', so use the tilde)

candidates.text: Judge allows Workday AI bias lawsuit to proceed as collective action
candidates.verified_how: Article opened live (fetch) today; title and page H1 match exactly. Body includes, verbatim: 'The applicant and four opt-in plaintiffs said they received hundreds of quick rejections without interviews for jobs via Workday, in violation of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act.' Not in the deck; no local file.
candidates.why_it_fits: Direct AI-hiring headline for 'no one wants me': an AI applicant-screening system is accused of rejecting older job seekers without interviews. Allegations only, not a finding; Workday says the claims lack merit. Use the headline as written; the 'hundreds of quick rejections' line can be a second card. Later 2026 rulings reported by law blogs were not opened and should not be on screen unless checked.

candidates.text: Finance worker pays out $25 million after video call with deepfake ‘chief financial officer’
candidates.verified_how: Article opened live (fetch) today; page title and headline match exactly ('... | CNN' suffix dropped). Body: Hong Kong police said the worker 'was duped into attending a video call with what he thought were several other members of staff, but all of whom were in fact deepfake recreations'; HK$200 million (about $25.6 million). Not in the deck; no local file. Trim option if needed: keep full headline (about 13 words) rather than cutting 'chief financial officer'.
candidates.why_it_fits: Strongest deepfake-of-real-people example for 'the way I'm perceived': a fake version of colleagues and the CFO on a video call fooled a worker. Police-sourced, widely reported, and the headline is exact. For a sharper 1-line alternate, use CNN 2024-05-16 'British engineering giant Arup revealed as $25 million deepfake scam victim' (https://www.cnn.com/2024/05/16/tech/arup-deepfake-scam-loss-hong-kong-intl-hnk/index.html; verified live; Arup spokesperson: 'we can confirm that fake voices and images were used').
